clue.text: Elegant society girl is broad, casting

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, a young woman entering high society
read together as 'is broadcasting', which is being on air

explanation.surface: A well-dressed debutante is described as broad and in the middle of casting something.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits 'broadcasting' in two to hide the phrase; a programme being broadcast is ON AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes a suave, stylish manner, so it is a synonym of elegant.

clue.text: Spruce padre moving piano inside

indicators.note: inside says the musical letter goes within the rearranged letters
moving the letters of the clergyman word shifts them into a new order

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A neat clergyman shifts a piano indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges PADRE to DAPER; 'inside' puts P within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce means neat and smart in appearance, as a well-turned-out man is.

clue.text: Security that is for a magistrate in Dundee

parts.note: bail is money given as security for release
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A guarantee intended for a Scottish judge.
explanation.walkthrough: Dundee is a Scottish city, signalling the Scots word for a town magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailie is a municipal magistrate or councillor in Scotland.

clue.text: Winter pear for one with 50 more first inside seen in retrospect

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round
in retrospect means looking back, so the word for seen is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: more first says the extra fifty is put ahead of the one

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A seasonal fruit for someone, with more added, viewed looking back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retrospect' turns SEEN to NEES; LI goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelis or nelies is the name of a variety of pear that ripens late in the year.

clue.text: Surly niece cavorted in a dangerous way

indicators.note: cavorted means leapt about, so the letters dance into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A grumpy niece pranced around recklessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Insecurely means unsafely or precariously, likely to fall or fail.

clue.text: Youngster expecting perhaps a chubby-faced child

definitions.text: Youngster expecting perhaps a chubby-faced child

parts.words: Youngster expecting perhaps a chubby-faced child
parts.note: the whole clue describes a plump angelic infant, the sort of baby a young mother-to-be pictures

explanation.definitionFit: Cherubs are painted as chubby winged infants, and the word is used for any sweet round-faced little child.

clue.text: Be still twice as confidential

indicators.note: twice says the word for be still is written two times

parts.note: hush means be quiet or still

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay silent, doubly so because it is secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Hush-hush means highly secret, kept quiet.

clue.text: Recollected having been sum-mened again

explanation.definitionFit: Recalled means remembered, and also called back a second time.

clue.text: Outlaws a group of musicians who have it both ways

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
taken as written

indicators.note: both ways says the little word appears forwards and then backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Criminals are like a band who want to have it both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface idiom 'have it both ways' disguises the instruction: the one 'it' is used twice, once read normally and once read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditti is the Italian-derived plural of bandit, a gang of robbers.

clue.text: It does not hurt for father to be out more

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
someone who is out more often is, put the other way, in less

explanation.surface: A remark that dad's absence from home causes nobody any pain.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is whimsical: if Pa is out more, he is IN LESS, giving PA + IN + LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something painless causes no suffering, so it does no harm or injury.

clue.text: Mum, after one, is able to find a refuse container

indicators.note: after says the hushing word comes behind the single letter for one

parts.note: a means one, as in a single thing
mum as in 'keep mum' means be quiet, hence the call SH
can means is able to

explanation.surface: Mother, following someone, manages to locate a rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother but is the instruction to keep quiet, SH.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashcan is an American term for a dustbin, a bin for household rubbish.

clue.text: Height of fame

definitions.meaning: a raised piece of ground, an elevation
distinction or high standing in public esteem

explanation.definitionFit: Eminence means both a hill or high place and lofty rank or renown.

clue.text: What is hot to the tongue and cold to the ear?

definitions.text: What is hot to the tongue

indicators.note: to the ear asks for a word that sounds the same as a synonym for cold

parts.note: chilly means cold

explanation.surface: A riddle about something both hot and cold at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The riddle form disguises a homophone: the hot pepper sounds like the word for cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilli peppers are fiery spices that burn the mouth when eaten.

clue.text: Is able to see well into the future despite having defective vision

definitions.text: Is able to see well into the future

definitions.meaning: long-sighted, unable to focus on near things

explanation.definitionFit: Far-sighted means prudent and forward-looking, and also hypermetropic, seeing distant things better than close ones.

clue.text: Newspaper covering a double bed?

definitions.meaning: humorously, a wide piece of bedlinen

explanation.definitionFit: A broadsheet is a full-size newspaper, and read literally it is a broad sheet for a big bed.

clue.text: Performed each differently

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Performed each differently': anagram of EACH gives only four letters; a fodder word (apparently DIVE) is missing from the OCR and no scan or search supplies it

clue.text: Creeper from Canada on form

indicators.note: form as a verb means shape, so the letters are moulded into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A climbing plant from Canada in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creeper' suggests a plant, but it is a snake; 'form' rearranges CANADA ON.
explanation.definitionFit: An anaconda is a huge South American snake, which crawls along the ground.

clue.text: One protects the viewer from strong light

definitions.text: One protects the viewer from strong light

parts.words: One protects the viewer from strong light
parts.note: describes a visor that shields the eyes, the viewer being an eye

explanation.definitionFit: An eyeshade is a visor worn on the forehead to shield the eyes from glare.

clue.text: Stick in something sweet and sticky

definitions.text: Stick in something sweet and sticky

parts.words: Stick in something sweet and sticky
parts.note: describes a fairground treat of spun sugar wrapped around a wooden stick

explanation.definitionFit: Candyfloss is spun sugar served on a stick at fairs, sweet and tacky to touch.

clue.text: Girl to finish in her underwear

indicators.note: in says the finishing word goes inside the garment

parts.note: a bra is a woman's undergarment
end means to finish

explanation.surface: A young woman finishing off while in her underclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Brenda is a woman's first name, and crosswords use girl for any female name.

clue.text: Happen to be in season

parts.note: tide is an old word for a season, as in Yuletide

explanation.surface: Something may occur when it is in its proper time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link here, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To betide means to befall or occur, as in 'woe betide'.

clue.text: Henry taking number a dis upward

annotationWithheld.clue: Henry taking number a dis upward

clue.text: Lest it has been packed

definitions.meaning: for fear that, as a precaution
literally, inside a box or suitcase

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'as a precaution' and, read literally, sitting inside a suitcase.

clue.text: Give rage in order to afflict

indicators.note: putting the letters in order means arranging them afresh

explanation.surface: Advice to vent anger so as to cause someone distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' signals rearranging GIVE RAGE into a new word.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve is to wrong or distress someone, causing them trouble or grief.

clue.text: Wrecker left museum first

indicators.note: first puts the museum ahead of the letter for left

parts.note: the V and A is London's Victoria and Albert Museum

explanation.surface: Someone destructive departed, having visited a museum beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London; spelled out it gives V AND A.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal deliberately damages property, a destroyer of things.

clue.text: Permanent position in society

explanation.definitionFit: Standing as an adjective means fixed and lasting; as a noun it means rank or repute.

clue.text: Prize returned by artist

indicators.note: returned means the word for prize is turned back to front

parts.note: a reward is a prize

explanation.surface: A trophy given back by a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns REWARD backwards to make DRAWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawer is one who draws, a sketcher or illustrator.

clue.text: A disc-jockey has a little money next door

parts.note: DJ is the usual short form of disc jockey
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: A radio presenter has some small change and lives next door.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjacent means neighbouring or lying alongside, as a house beside another does.
